turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi, Mr.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Whittaker.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm Megan Cowalczyk, the nurse practitioner in the heart failure clinic. Can you confirm your full name and date of birth for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Darnell Whittaker, February 27th, 1958.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thank you. The nurse said you called on Monday about some swelling.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: What's been happening? Yeah, my ankles have been puffing up for about a week. My shoes are tight by the afternoon, and the scale says I'm up seven pounds.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay. What's your usual weight at home?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm usually right around 182. This morning it was 189.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And how's your breathing? Worse than usual,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: normally I can walk three blocks to the corner store. Now I'm winded after about one block.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How many pillows are you sleeping on? I've gone from one pillow to two,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: feels easier to breathe propped up. Are you waking up at night, gasping for air? No, not that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any chest pain, or feeling like you might pass out?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No chest pain, no passing out.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Anything different with your diet, the last couple of weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well, my nephew got married two weekends ago. There was a lot of ham, a lot of salty food. I wasn't careful, I'll admit it. my wife Lorraine already gave me an earful. That happens.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's go through your medicines. You're on Sacubitrol Valsartin, 49, and 51 milligrams twice a day. Carve it along 12 .5 milligrams twice a day. Spire nalactone 25 milligrams once a day, and Dapagliflazin 10 milligrams once a day, still taking all of those. Rose.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Every one of them, Lorraine fills my pill box on Sundays.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And the furose mind. How much are you taking?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The water pill is 20 milligrams in the morning. Wait no, it's the 40.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: They changed it in the summer, it's 40.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: 40 milligrams once a day is what I have, anything over the counter.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Um, I've been taking naproxen for my knees. The arthritis acts up two of the 220 milligram pills twice a day for about two weeks.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, that's important.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'll come back to that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let me check you over. Your weight here is 189 pounds. Blood pressure is 112 over 70, pulse 78, and oxygen is 95 % on room air. your neck veins are up to about 10 centimeters. I hear some crackles at the bottom of both lungs. Heart is regular and I hear a soft extra sound called an S3 and you've got two -plus pitting swelling up to the middle of both shins.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That doesn't sound great.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It tells me you're holding onto extra fluid. Your last Last echo in March showed an ejection fraction of 30%, so your heart pump is weaker than normal, and it's sensitive to salt. Your labs from three weeks ago were okay, potassium -4,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: and create 9 .1 .2. So what do we do? So this is a mild flare of your heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. I think the salty food and the naproxen both played a part. Naproxen makes the kidneys hold onto salt and water, so I want you to stop it completely.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: What do I take for the knees then?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Acetaminophen is safer for your heart. You can take 650 milligrams, up to three times a day. For

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: the fluid,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm increasing the furose mind to 40 milligrams twice a day for the next five days. Once your weight is back near 183, go back to 40 milligrams once a day.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay 40 twice a day for five days.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Right, keep all your other heart medicines the same. way yourself every morning after you use the bathroom and write it down. Keep salt under 2 ,000 milligrams a day and fluids to about two liters.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Lorraine's going to love that she's been on me about the salt.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'd also like a basic metabolic panel on the 21st of October to make sure your kidneys and potassium are okay with the higher dose. Call us if your weight goes up 3 pounds in a day or 5 pounds in a week. If you're short of breath at rest or you get chest pain, go to the emergency room.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Got it!

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And are you using the patient portal?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I can send you the instructions there. Yes, it's darnell .widdaker at xamplemail .com.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Perfect. I'll send the plan there, and I want to see you back in one week to check your weight and the swelling.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sounds good. Thank you, Megan.
